site: ADP, Workday, and web-component comboboxes with lazy-mounted option lists
class: Concept option resolution against empty initial snapshot produces uncalibrated values that fail at pick time
symptom: When a dropdown has options=() in the initial ARIA snapshot, answer_what_is_known resolved concepts like WORK_AUTHORIZATION to generic 'Yes' and ETHNICITY_RACE to 'Asian'. When the menu opened at choose() time, option_match.best_option failed to match 'Yes' against sponsorship-qualified options ('Yes, with sponsorship' / 'Yes, without restrictions') or 'Asian' against Hispanic/Latino choices ('Not Hispanic or Latino'), causing form filling to fail and stalling the run.
root_cause: known_answer() evaluated confirm_concept() and resolve_profile_value() before dropdown choices were read. Without options, sponsorship and demographic disambiguation fell back to uncalibrated defaults. Furthermore, ADP's <sdf-select-simple> and <sdf-card> web components lacked dedicated adapter picker and inline card save hooks.
why_tests_missed: Existing blank dropdown tests only verified handing over choices to the LLM planner feedback loop, and did not test the deterministic zero-cost answer_what_is_known path resolving against live choices.
fix: In page_agent.py answer_what_is_known, pre-read closed combobox options for option-sensitive concepts before known_answer so resolve_profile_value receives the live option vocabulary. In _choose_exact, re-resolve against live options using confirm_concept and sponsorship_option when initial lookup misses. In sites/adp.py, implement open_picker, select_option, and commit_card hooks for ADP custom elements.
prevention: Ensure option-dependent concepts always receive real option vocabularies before committing form answers, and re-resolve against live dropdown rows when initial matching fails.
